issue: Does the First Step Act's amended § 924(c) penalty structure (§ 403(a)) apply at a resentencing where the original sentence was imposed before the Act but vacated, and does it matter whether the vacatur came before or after enactment?

sides.position: Section 403(a) applies at resentencing after vacatur, even where the original sentence was vacated before the First Step Act was enacted (Bethea holds this regardless of vacatur timing; Uriarte and Henry hold it where vacatur preceded enactment).
cases: United States v. Uriarte, 975 F.3d 596 (7th Cir. 2020) (en banc)
United States v. Henry, 983 F.3d 214 (6th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Bethea, 841 F. App'x 544 (4th Cir. 2021)

sides.position: Section 403(a) does not apply at a resentencing where the original sentence had already been vacated when the First Step Act was enacted.
cases: United States v. Hodge, 948 F.3d 160 (3d Cir. 2020)

quote: Our sister Circuits are divided on this question, and on the question of whether it matters if a defendant’s original sentence was vacated before or after the First Step Act was enacted.
cite: United States v. Eldridge, 2 F.4th 27 (2d Cir. 2021)
